title: Per-repository integration contract
description: One repository's deployment-facing contract: what it is, where its checkout comes from, how to prove it, and the named deployables it produces. A deployable is the unit profiles select and provision delivers; a repository may produce more than one, and several here produce both a device half and a server half of the same contract.

repository.description: The checkout directory name under the kit; preflight cross-checks it against the environment mapping's declared path.

unreal_project.description: Checkout-relative path to this integration's .uproject, declared only by integrations that own one. preflight reads its EngineAssociation and holds it against the engine the environment actually declares, so a project and its toolchain cannot drift apart unnoticed. Discovery would be worse than declaration here: a glob that finds no project passes silently, which is the exact failure this check exists to catch.

origin.description: The canonical clone source. bootstrap clones a missing checkout from it; an integration without one cannot be materialized, only reported.

domain.description: The Stack level this leaf sits under, and the level of the canonical workstation tree its checkout sits under.

prove.description: The repository's own test entry point, run by check. It proves the repository, not any one deployable, which is why it sits here.

deployables.description: Named deployables, keyed by the name the owning repository uses. A deployable with no build and no artifacts is a recorded absence: named, visibly unbuildable here, and honest about it.

command.description: A long-running serve or a health probe. argv may reference ${BUNDLE} (the member's staged artifact directory) and ${STATE} (a per-run writable root); the working directory is always ${STATE}. env is a non-secret overlay — the no-secrets rule applies to it in full.

destination.description: Where this deployable ends up. device and server are the reserved terminals; any other value names the member whose artifact carries it, and the chain is resolved to a terminal by the binding (D-19).

artifacts.description: Checkout-relative paths of the outputs build stages into a bundle. Never absolute, never escaping.
